archetype: Mardu Vampire typal go-wide linear aggro that kills by trigger rather than by combat: Edgar's eminence mints a body for every Vampire spell cast from the command zone, token multipliers stack on every mint, and SEVEN converters turn creature traffic into life loss from two directions at once — five entry payoffs (Purphoros, God of the Forge, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight, Witty Roastmaster) that fire when a body arrives, and two death drains (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant) that fire when a body leaves, so a resolved board wipe pays the pilot instead of ending the game. Combat is the second kill through the lord-and-anthem layer; two checker-passed lifegain/lifeloss infinites (Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or with Sanguine Bond; stacks 004 and 006) are a bonus route that assembles unassisted in 4.8% of games and is priced accordingly. The deck runs zero graveyard content by design, and the 99 is held fixed for a piloting-practice period, so this frame is a playing guide, not a shopping list.

role_assignment.default_role: The beatdown, assigned per-threat: four-player games trend long and inevitability compounds, so 'aggro must instead compress the game before the table's late game arrives' (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). This deck's compression is real — the go-wide kill (a token-to-damage payoff AND a multiplier) assembles by turn 6 in 41.7% of games, 57.7% with the three tutors — and roles are 'set by matchup and game state, not your deck's label' (strategy:whos-the-beatdown), so re-ask at every board change: you can be the control against a faster combo seat while staying the beatdown against the ramp player in the same turn cycle.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Concrete events, per strategy:pivot-point: a resolved sweeper flips the deck to rebuild-and-drain (eminence re-mints from the command zone, and the death drains mean the wipe itself paid you); the kill config assembling — converter plus multiplier, in hand in 57.4% of games at mean turn 4.2 — opens the all-in window. Take that window only when the attempt 'can't be profitably answered — protection up, table tapped out' or 'doesn't need to resolve fully to leave you ahead' (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window); the five free-or-flash protection spells are held for the turn you commit, not after.

engines.engine: Eminence token mint: every Vampire spell cast mints a 1/1 Vampire token, live from the command zone in 100% of games — the deck's ignition never has to be drawn or cast (the six-mana body itself is a late bonus, median cast turn 6 in goldfish).
engines.evidence: oracle text + verified stack 002 (eminence through two doublers: bodies per cast)

engines.engine: Entry-to-damage conversion, with Purphoros, God of the Forge, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight and Witty Roastmaster: each creature entry reaches every opponent at once, which is the answer to the 1-to-3 asymmetry — a converter is drawn in 73.5% of games, 62.6% by turn 6 (goldfish, seed 42).
engines.evidence: verified stack 009 (three payoffs compose on one two-mana Vampire cast) + verified stack 008 (Purphoros through the doublers)

engines.engine: Death drain, with Cruel Celebrant: every creature death — yours included — drains and pays the pilot, so the sweeper the table must eventually cast into this board converts to reach instead of a reset. Card-level nuance from oracle text: Blood Artist drains one target player per death; only Cruel Celebrant hits each opponent.

Token multiplication, with Mondrak, Glory Dominus, Ocelot Pride, Elspeth, Storm Slayer and the token makers: replacement doublers stack multiplicatively on every eminence mint and every token producer — the deck's healthiest component, drawn in 78.9% of games.
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 (two doublers stacking) + goldfish multiplier target 0.789

engines.engine: The combat layer: lords, +1/+1 counters and Shared Animosity turn the same width into attack lethality, and Sanctum Seeker makes each attacking Vampire itself a drain — a lord or anthem is drawn in 78.9% of games.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (Sanctum Seeker attack drain math) + goldfish lord/anthem target 0.789

engines.engine: The drain infinite: with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond, a lifegain/lifeloss loop kills the table at zero additional mana. Both pairings are checker-passed and both are two-card lines resting on this single body — 7.1% of opening sevens, 4.8% assembled unassisted, 24.3% with tutors — which is the declared ceiling on the line, not a defect.
engines.evidence: combo_details (both lines contained, infinite, mana_value_needed 0, popularity 64,824 and 54,630) + verified stacks 004 and 006

engines.engine: Drain doubler: opponents' life loss during your turn is doubled, turning a Sanctum Seeker attack that hurts into one that kills. A one-card line (5.2% assembled) whose {1}{B}{B}{B} is the only triple-B cost in the 99 — the hardest cast in the deck's shortest colour.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (attack math) + verified stack 007 (Throne of the God-Pharaoh end step: what doubles and what does not)

engines.engine: Width-scaling draw, with Champion of Dusk, Pact of the Serpent, Preacher of the Schism, Welcoming Vampire, Caretaker's Talent and Night's Whisper: the refill is priced in life and bodies — resources this deck banks by the handful — and never touches a graveyard. A draw engine is drawn in 73.4% of games, 62.2% by turn 6.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The wipe pays the pilot: exact drain total when a sweeper resolves through Blood Artist + Cruel Celebrant with Vito on board
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: each death triggers each drain, each drain's lifegain triggers Vito's target-opponent loss, and the ordering of simultaneous deaths under a wipe is exactly the multi-trigger math a checker should audit — the frame claims a wipe converts to reach, and the claim deserves a verified number.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Does Bloodletter double the death drains under an OPPONENT'S sweeper?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Bloodletter's doubling reads 'during your turn' — so the wipe-insurance line is doubled when you wipe on your own turn (Olivia's Wrath) but plausibly NOT when the table wipes on theirs. The timing boundary is precisely checker fodder, and it changes what a held Olivia's Wrath is worth.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Assume the wrath — 'over a four-player game one is near-certain' — and buy 'resilience instead of restraint' (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). This 99 buys resilience twice: five free-or-flash protection spells (held by turn 6 in 50.0% of games), and the death drains, which make the resolved wipe itself drain the table as the board dies. Commit in waves anyway: eminence is the rebuild package that never leaves the command zone, so 'redeploy worst-first, keeping the best threat in hand for their second sweeper' costs this deck less than any other aggro list at the table.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes hit 'decks built on many cheap spells per turn' hardest (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial), and this deck is exactly that — 29 spell entries at MV 2 or less. Recount the hand under the tax: a two-spell turn becoming one halves the eminence engine. Role is forced: 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion.' Name the piece that beats YOU — usually the one taxing creature entries or preventing life loss — and spend the eight true answers (Anguished Unmaking, Despark, Generous Gift, Path to Exile, Stroke of Midnight, Swords to Plowshares, Winds of Abandon, Elspeth's -3) on that piece, not the scariest one.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Duke's operational tests decide the mirror: 'who has inevitability... who is faster' (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). This deck usually keeps the beatdown seat while gaining a defence: the converters kill without a combat step and every drain raises your total as it lowers theirs, pushing the opposing aggro deck's damage-per-card rate below lethal — strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire prices exactly this, 'every extra card you force the aggressor to spend... comes from a finite stock.' Assign per-threat: beatdown against one seat, control against another, in the same turn cycle.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: The 99 holds no stack interaction, so the only lever is the clock: 'aggro must compress the game before the table's late game arrives' (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The kill config lands by turn 6 in 41.7% of games, 57.7% tutor-assisted — that is the race, and the tutors should buy the missing kill half, not infinite pieces. When you present lethal, 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing' (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window); prefer the attack-plus-triggers kill that leaves a rebuilt board if it fails over an all-in loop that does not.

distribution_notes: Copies, not entries: 100 copies across 97 entries — 37 land copies in 34 entries, 63 spells. Curve (nonland) 12 / 17 / 21 / 7 / 5 / 1 across mana values 1-6, modal 3, nothing at 7+, with eleven Vampires at MV 2 or less feeding eminence. Roles: threat:body 29 (inside the aggro 26-32 band), threat:tokens 10, doubler:tokens 3, wincon:drain 9, wincon:combat 4; taxonomy coverage 100%. Goldfish (seed 42, 10K games): keep 80.8% of first sevens, turn-3 land drop 91.9%, mean bodies 4.2 by turn 6. The binding axis is black mana: 39 B pips across 29 cards — nearly half the deck's coloured demand — on 27 sources against the Karsten double-pip target of 36, for 76.4% on-curve black castability with rocks against the 90% standard (strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources: 'his 99-card column assumes 40 lands, on the play, casting on curve, "consistently" ≈ 90%'), and the drain payoffs are the black cards, so the shortage taxes the kill, not the filler. Interaction: 8 enumerated true answers across creature/artifact/enchantment/land, graveyard zero — Takenuma, Abandoned Mire is the only graveyard-touching text in the 99 and it targets your own yard. Protection 7 copies at the top of the 5-7 band. One sweeper, Olivia's Wrath, correct for the deck that owns the board — with a named friction: five of the 29 creatures are not Vampires (Corpse Knight, Mondrak, Ocelot Pride, Witty Roastmaster, and Purphoros when devotion animates it), so the deck's own wipe hits two converters and both nonland doubler bodies, though the death drains collect on the way down. Cavern of Souls' coloured mana casts creature spells only — it cannot pay Castle Locthwain's draw, Bloodline Keeper's flip cost or Captivating Vampire's activation. Midgar, City of Mako contributes B only on its front face. Bracket floor 4 (Optimized) on four Game Changers plus the two contained two-card infinites. The synergy graph's 55 intra-deck edges are a global top-10 shortlist, not a per-deck fit score, and contribute nothing to this frame's engine claims.
overall_assessment: This is a linear critical-mass deck (strategy:critical-mass) whose threshold is a number of creature entries, and whose defining property is that those entries pay from BOTH directions: arriving, through five entry converters, and dying, through two death drains. The entry half is the answer to strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's charge against aggro — '~120 combined life behind three defenses makes incremental combat damage a losing plan... each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale' — and stack 009 verifies it on the deck's own terms: three payoffs composing on one two-mana Vampire cast is the primary plan as rules-fact. The death half rewrites the linear deck's classic weakness: strategy:critical-mass warns that 'interaction slots are the price of the engine, so the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers,' and strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math says to 'buy resilience instead of restraint... threats that replace themselves' — here the resilience is that the near-certain table wipe drains opponents as the board dies, and then eminence rebuilds from a zone no wipe touches. The frame prices cards as quanta of damage (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire), and the goldfish says the machine runs: converter 62.6% by turn 6, multiplier 68.2%, both together 41.7% unassisted and 57.7% with tutors, draw engine 62.2% keeping the hand full. The infinites are found money, not the plan: strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices a named card at '7.1% of your opening seven,' and every loop routes through Bloodthirsty Conqueror (4.8% assembled) or Bloodletter's lone triple-B cast (5.2%) — race with the entries, spend the three tutors on the missing kill half by default, and present a loop only into a window strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window would sanction. Two tensions are live: black is the short colour under the heaviest pip load (27 of 36 Karsten sources, 76.4% on-curve), and it is the colour of the drains; and graveyard is the one uncovered interaction class, so a reanimator seat must be answered by clock, not by cards. The 99 is held fixed for a piloting-practice period, which fits the deck's real skill ceiling: role re-assignment, wave deployment under sweeper math, and pivot timing are where games are won with this exact list.
gaps: No section on death-trigger value engines (aristocrats): the doc prices sweeper commitment (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) and life-as-currency, but has no school for decks whose own board dying is a payoff — this frame stretched wrath-math's 'resilience instead of restraint' clause to cover wipe-insurance-as-archetype.
No section on typal density: lord count versus creature count versus removal exposure has no doc target, so the combat layer is sized by goldfish measurement alone.

No section on command-zone engines (eminence and other uncast commander value): strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance covers the recast tax, which this deck's engine never pays — an ignition that cannot be interacted with deserves its own theory.
